name: Analytical Content Management & Collaboration
rationale: The semantics and lifecycle are real, but independent cross-provider adoption, economics, exit and support remain too weak for a sovereign product boundary.

adoption.finding: Tableau projects, Power BI workspaces and Jupyter collaboration are adopted with their containing products; independent replacement is not proven.
adoption.subject: analytical_content_collaboration

authority.finding: Container access and collaboration moderation are distinct from artifact authorship, semantic approval, formal issuance and business decision authority.
authority.subject: analytical_content_collaboration

economics.finding: No independently adopted cross-provider analytical content control plane with isolated pricing and support was proven in this pass.
economics.subject: analytical_content_collaboration

interface.finding: Generic annotation and version-control contracts exist, while a portable heterogeneous analytical-content export contract remains unselected.
interface.subject: analytical_content_collaboration

job.finding: Organize, share, govern, review, discuss and locate heterogeneous analytical artifacts without owning their internal semantics.
job.subject: analytical_content_collaboration

lifecycle.finding: Containers, memberships, threads, reviews and release collections have state, but artifact lifecycle remains with each producer product.
lifecycle.subject: analytical_content_collaboration

market_evidence.finding: Multiple suites converge on the state model, but convergence proves reusable seams rather than independent product economics.
market_evidence.subject: analytical_content_collaboration

operation.finding: Cross-artifact indexing, access projection, collaboration synchronization and retention are operable, though commonly bundled.
operation.subject: analytical_content_collaboration

semantics.finding: Container, membership, ownership, content reference, edition link, annotation anchor, comment thread, review and packaged release are reusable meanings.
semantics.subject: analytical_content_collaboration

user.finding: Content administrators, authors, reviewers and consumers are distinguishable, but usually operate inside a containing analytical product.
user.subject: analytical_content_collaboration

adoption.finding: Knock and Novu expose independently adoptable notification workflow products; provider/channel services can be replaced behind them.
adoption.subject: notification_orchestration_delivery

authority.finding: The product owns bounded communication-delivery authority, never source truth, analytical threshold, business acceptance or incident disposition.
authority.subject: notification_orchestration_delivery

economics.finding: Notification orchestration is independently priced, capacity-managed, supported and exited across applications.
economics.subject: notification_orchestration_delivery

interface.finding: Typed trigger APIs, workflow definitions, preference APIs, provider ports and delivery receipts form explicit adoption and exit surfaces.
interface.subject: notification_orchestration_delivery

job.finding: Turn typed communication intents into preference-aware, policy-bounded, multi-channel delivery attempts and receipts.
job.subject: notification_orchestration_delivery

lifecycle.finding: Workflow, schedule, trigger, attempt, suppression and delivery outcome have independent state machines.
lifecycle.subject: notification_orchestration_delivery

market_evidence.finding: At least two independent implementation families converge on workflow, preference, schedule and multi-channel delivery state.
market_evidence.subject: notification_orchestration_delivery

operation.finding: Routing, batching, throttling, retry, provider fallback, rate limits, observability and replay require an independent runtime.
operation.subject: notification_orchestration_delivery

semantics.finding: Workflow edition, trigger occurrence, recipient projection, preference snapshot, template edition, schedule, delivery attempt and outcome are first-class state.
semantics.subject: notification_orchestration_delivery

user.finding: Notification platform engineers and communication operators are distinct from analytical authors and business decision owners.
user.subject: notification_orchestration_delivery

reason: Alert rule, evaluation, subscription, notification workflow, delivery attempt, interaction receipt and escalation do not share one owner, consistency boundary or authority.
